before.name: South Side Route
before.overview: The quickest and busiest line on the mountain, a plain and fairly short climb up the south slope. Slow parties tend to bottleneck beneath the bergschrund, and newcomers should not underestimate it despite its easy reputation.
before.detailed_rack: Kit depends heavily on season. Favorable conditions may need only a lightweight axe and crampons; tougher ones can justify an additional axe or technical tool, plus a rope and protection. Usual items: crampons, axe, belay device, harness, pickets, rope.
before.approach: Start at Timberline Lodge and walk the marked path up the right side of the ski area, avoiding the ground under the lifts. Head straight up toward the right side of Crater Rock. The Devil's Kitchen is a large flat area on the way and the usual rest stop. Above it is the Hogsback, the saddle between Crater Rock and the summit; fumaroles near it can release toxic gas.
before.descent_text: Descend the way you came up, taking care because conditions can change quickly.

keptBefore.name: South Side (Hogsback)
gear: Glacier rope and crevasse rescue kit if roping up
hazards: Rockfall and icefall from Crater Rock and the Steel Cliff
Fumarole holes and toxic gas near Devil's Kitchen and the Hot Rocks
Long sliding falls on hard or icy snow
keptBefore.overview: The most-climbed route on Oregon's highest peak, starting from the lodge on its south flank and following the ski area, then a snow ridge between steaming fumaroles, to the summit ridge. Most of it is a long snow walk, but the last thousand feet is steep, exposed snow above a bergschrund with rockfall and icefall from the surrounding cliffs. It is usually done in one long day with a very early start.
keptBefore.beta: From the top of the ski area, climb the snowfield toward the prominent dark buttress of Crater Rock and pass it on its east (climber's right) side, above the sulfur-smelling fumarole area of Devil's Kitchen, to reach the Hogsback, a narrow snow ridge on the north side of Crater Rock that leads up toward the summit cliffs. Put crampons on at its base. The Hogsback ends below a bergschrund that crosses the slope; how it is passed changes through the season. Above it, the Pearly Gates are a narrow, Y-shaped gully through the rime-coated rock straight ahead; they are the most direct finish but are often icy or melted out. The more common finish now is the Old Chute: from the low point on the Hogsback crest, drop slightly to the north side and climb a broad steep face into a narrowing chute through the summit cliffs, steepening to around 45° before topping out on the summit ridge. Walk the ridge east to the true summit, staying well back from cornices overhanging the north face.
keptBefore.turnaround: Set a firm turnaround time and be off the steep upper slopes before the sun loosens rime and rock from the cliffs above; many parties aim to summit by mid-morning and turn around by late morning at the latest. Turn back at the Hogsback if the bergschrund crossing looks unsound, the snow is soft and wet, or the upper mountain is in cloud.
keptBefore.rock_grade: Steep snow to about 45° in the Old Chute; glacier travel near the top
obj_haz: Rime and rock released from the cliffs as the sun hits them
Snow bridges over the bergschrund and fumaroles weakening through the day
Sulfur gas pooling in the fumarole areas, enough to suffocate someone who falls into a vent
Crowds on the steep chutes sending down ice and loose snow

waypoints.name: Timberline Lodge
waypoints.directions: From US 26 just east of Government Camp, turn north on Timberline Road and drive about 6 miles to the parking lots at Timberline Lodge. Fill out the free self-issued wilderness permit at the climbers' register in the Wy'east Day Lodge before starting. An Oregon Sno-Park permit is required to park from November through April.

waypoints.name: Mount Hood
waypoints.directions: Take the climbers' trail on the east edge of the ski runs past the Silcox Hut and the top of the Palmer lift at about 8,500 ft. Continue up the snowfield toward Crater Rock, past Devil's Kitchen and the Hot Rocks, and swing around its east side to the base of the Hogsback. Follow the snow ridge to the bergschrund, climb the Old Chute to the summit ridge, and walk east to the top.

what_to_bring: Mt. Hood climbing permit for travel above 9,500 ft
Wilderness permit and climber registration, filled out at the lodge
Oregon Sno-Park permit to park at Timberline from November through April
Warm layers, shell and goggles for wind at the top
Food and water for a 10 to 14 hour day
pro_tips: Go midweek to avoid lines in the chutes
Start between about 1 and 3 AM to be back below Crater Rock before the sun loosens the cliffs
Check the current conditions report; the finish that is in shape changes through the season
Save a track or bearing on the way up for the descent
keptBefore.watch_out:
Descending in cloud, the fall line pulls parties toward the Zigzag Glacier and Mississippi Head or into White River Canyon
Do not rope together without anchors on the steep chutes; one fall can pull the whole team off
Keep clear of snowcats and ski traffic in the ski area
Afternoon warming turns firm snow to slush and increases rockfall
keptBefore.best_season: April through June, when a firm, freeze-thawed snowpack covers the upper mountain and the bergschrund is usually still bridged. Later in summer the upper slopes melt out into loose rock and ice, and rockfall and crevasse problems grow.
keptBefore.approach: From the parking lot at Timberline Lodge, head north past the lodge to the marked climbers' trail, which follows the east edge of the ski runs. The Silcox Hut is roughly a thousand feet above the start. Keep climbing on the east side of the groomed runs and out of the way of snowcats and skiers, up past the top of the Palmer lift at about 8,500 ft. Above that, continue up the snowfield toward Crater Rock, passing the steaming fumarole area of Devil's Kitchen and the Hot Rocks, and swing around the east side of Crater Rock to the base of the Hogsback.
keptBefore.descent_text: Descend the way you came, most parties reversing the Old Chute facing into the slope, then down the Hogsback and around Crater Rock to the ski area and back to the lodge. In poor visibility, a compass bearing that does not account for the fall line will pull descending parties off to the southwest onto the Zigzag Glacier and toward Mississippi Head, or southeast toward White River Canyon; carry a planned bearing or track and follow it carefully.
keptBefore.bail: Crater Rock and the top of the ski area are the natural retreat points; below the Hogsback the terrain is a long moderate snow slope back to the lodge. Retreating from the Old Chute or Pearly Gates means downclimbing steep snow facing in, so decide before committing to the chute.

pitch_detail.notes: Climbers' trail on the east side of the ski runs, past the Silcox Hut to about 8,500 ft. Watch for snowcats and skiers.
pitch_detail.pitch: Timberline Lodge to top of Palmer

pitch_detail.notes: Open snowfield toward the dark buttress of Crater Rock; pass Devil's Kitchen and the Hot Rocks, whose fumaroles give off sulfur gas.
Pass Crater Rock on its east side and gain the base of the Hogsback. Put crampons on here.
pitch_detail.pitch: Around Crater Rock to the Hogsback

pitch_detail.notes: Narrow snow ridge leading up toward the bergschrund below the summit cliffs. Fumarole holes open on either side as the season goes on.
Cross the bergschrund area, then climb the Old Chute to the summit ridge. The Pearly Gates go straight up the narrow gully ahead and are often icy or melted out. Exposed to rockfall and icefall.
Short walk east to the summit. Stay back from cornices over the north face.

access.fees: $20 for 3 days or $50 annual; wilderness permit and registration free
access.permit: Mt. Hood climbing permit (required above 9,500 ft, year-round) plus a free wilderness permit and climber registration at the lodge
access.land_manager: Mt. Hood National Forest (Mount Hood Wilderness above the ski area)
access.parking_pass: Oregon Sno-Park permit, November 1 to April 30

road.name: Timberline Highway
road.driveNote: Drive to Government Camp on US-26 and take the Timberline Highway up to the lodge parking lots.

keptBefore.rope_note: Many parties climb unroped because a rope team without protection on the steep chutes can turn one slip into a team fall. A rope is useful for the bergschrund crossing and fumarole holes later in the season, and for teams with less experience on glaciers.

keptBefore.name: East Ridge
keptBefore.overview: A well-established trail leads from the parking lot, meeting the PCT after 1.1 miles. Continue on the climbers trail past a second PCT junction (heading north) by staying straight. About 3 miles of good flowing trail precede the technical ground, where rocky footing, big step-ups and big drops lead to the East Ridge. Plod up the ridge to the last 600ft, a scree (or snow) slope ending at a large, pointed summit.
keptBefore.approach: From the trailhead parking lot a good trail runs about a mile to the first Pacific Crest Trail junction. Stay on the McLoughlin climbers trail, go straight past a second PCT junction that leads north, and follow smooth trail for a few miles before the footing turns rocky, with large step-ups. The well-worn trail leads to the East Ridge itself, and the final slope to the pointed summit is scree or snow.
